title: Best boys basketball players in San Joaquin County? Here are the Top 25 to watch in 2025-26 - NewsBreak
text:
By Dylan Ackermann ,
11 hours ago Talk about a casting decision no director wants to make.
Like actors stepping into the spotlight, San Joaquin County’s top basketball players deliver highlight-worthy performances every time they take the floor. Sorting through this star power took rewinding film, studying roles and identifying who owns the biggest moments.
The 209 never lacks talent — big-time scorers, crafty creators, deadeye shooters, high-level passers, tone-setting defenders and prospects who draw college attention like paparazzi flashes.
With the season just getting underway, fans, students and parents are settling in as the valley’s brightest stage lights flip on. Here’s The Record’s ranking of the Top 25 players poised to own the screen — or, really, the hardwood — this winter.
(Athletes listed in alphabetical order)
Jayden Akuva High School: Venture Academy
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: A 6-foot guard, Jayden Akuva is an efficient scorer with a reliable 3-point shot and a variety of finishes at the rim. He defends the full length of the floor and wreaks havoc on anyone trying to initiate offense, using strong lateral quickness to stay in front, cut off angles and jump passing lanes. Akuva averaged 9.9 points last season while shooting 52% from the field and 43% from 3-point range.
Eddie Andeola High School: Bear Creek
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Eddie Andeola spent last season carving up defenses from beyond the arc, sinking 51 threes — a mark that placed him inside the county’s top 10. Now stepping in as Bear Creek’s primary option, he’s positioned to let it fly even more. The 5-foot-10 guard averaged 10.1 points per game last season.
Romello Bruhn High School: Weston Ranch
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: One of the most prolific scorers in Sac-Joaquin Section history has moved to Stockton. With 2,472 career points, the 6-foot-3 guard is on pace to become just the 14th player in California history to reach 3,000. Last season, Romello Bruhn averaged 31 points and led Woodland Christian to its first Sac-Joaquin Section championship, scoring 49 points in an 87-63 win over Argonaut on Feb. 28. The stat sheet shines, but the eye test is even louder — Bruhn’s handle is silky, his jumper is cleaner and he gets to his spots whenever he wants. With effortless three-level his game should translate instantly to Division I. He also averaged 3.8 steals per game.
Amos Cady High School: Ripon Christian
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: If Amos Cady ever needed a nickname, “the triple-double flirter” would fit perfectly. What makes it even more impressive is that basketball isn’t even his primary sport. The 6-foot-2 Ripon Christian guard did it all last season — 14.8 points on 41% shooting, 6.4 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 3.1 steals — stuffing every corner of the stat sheet en route to being named the Trans Valley League’s Most Outstanding Player.
Damarcus Cobb High School: Weston Ranch
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: The definition of a big guard, Damarcus Cobb is a four-year varsity player who can impact the game in multiple ways. His talent and competitive edge make him a threat on both ends, but his pure strength and ability to get teammates involved stand out most. At 6-foot-4, Cobb averaged 10 points per game last season and will step into a larger leadership role this year.
Tristen DeBenedetti High School: Kimball
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Twenty-three points on Manteca. Twenty points on Modesto Christian. Tristen DeBenedetti showed last season that the scoring pop is real; now the question is consistency. After averaging 9.5 points per game, the 6-foot-2 senior now grabs the reins as Kimball’s most likely go-to scorer.
Idrees Elfarra High School: River Island
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: The midrange is where Idrees Elfarra goes to work. His step-backs, hesitations and spin moves carve out pockets of space, and a convincing ball fake keeps defenses guessing. The 5-foot-10 senior averaged 15.3 points and 4.1 assists per game last season.
Jayden Hinkston High School: St. Mary's
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Coming off a second-team All-TCAL campaign, Jayden Hinkston enters his senior season as St. Mary’s leading scorer and playmaker, after posting 11.7 points and 2.2 assists per game. His breakout night came on Dec. 5, 2024, when he poured in 22 points against Milpitas. Coaches say he’s taken another leap this summer. “Jayden has the ability to score at all three levels and has proven to be an elite on-ball defender,” St. Mary's coach Scooter Bloom said.
Mekhi Jefferson High School: Edison
Position/Year: Forward, Junior
Summary: A relentless rebounder who is still raw but loaded with intangibles, Mekhi Jefferson is a 6-foot-6 forward who controls the paint on both ends. He averaged a county-best 10.3 rebounds per game last season, including an impressive four on the offensive end. His stat line reads like a rebounding clinic: multiple 12-board games, a pair of 14s, two 15s and a dominant 16-rebound performance. And when he’s not cleaning the glass, he’s shutting down the rim — highlighted by a six-block outing and two more four-block efforts in his final three games.
Lorenzo Jones High School: East Union
Position/Year: Forward, Senior
Summary: Despite standing 6-foot-1 and weighing 170 pounds, the junior forward plays with the presence of a much bigger athlete. Last season he became a walking double-double, finishing just shy of averaging 10 points and 10 rebounds while securing All-VOL second-team recognition. "He has only gotten better and expanded his game,” East Union coach Dalton Ell said. “He is the best offensive rebounder in the area, bar none. High motor and will outwork anyone.”
Ayande Johnson High School: East Union
Position/Year: Guard, Junior
Summary: One hundred points in three JV games — that was Ayande Johnson’s introduction, and it didn’t take long for East Union to push him up the ladder. The junior guard can score from anywhere on the floor and shoots it with uncommon confidence. “One of the best shooters in the area,” Ell said. “He will have a ton of responsibility on this team.”
Josiah Johnson High School: Venture Academy
Position/Year: Guard, Junior
Summary: At just 5-foot-9, Josiah Johnson may be one of the smaller guards in the area, but he plays with a rhythm and confidence that quickly erases any size concerns. The left-handed guard brings pace, creativity and a handle that keeps defenders guessing. His energy is infectious and his competitiveness sets the tone. Johnson averaged 10 points per game and nearly two steals last season.
Habib Khan High School: Tokay
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Call him what the kids do — a bucket. Tokay senior Habib Khan exploded last year, pouring in 19 points a night and dropping a school-record 47 against Edison on Jan. 24. The 6-foot-4 guard led the Tigers to their first playoff appearance in over 10 years and earned first-team all-league honors along the way. Now closing in on 1,000 career points, Khan has already caught the eyes of several local junior colleges.
Jabril Lewis-Muhammad High School: Venture Academy
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: A physical 6-foot-3 guard who embraces contact, Jabril Lewis-Muhammad has strong balance and excels at playing off two feet. His downhill ability allows him to stop on a dime and get to his midrange jumper, while also making him a capable 3-point shooter. Lewis-Muhammad averaged 10.4 points per game last season.
Charles Mapanao High School: River Island
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Charles Mapanao can flat-out shoot it. His 94 made 3-pointers last season ranked fifth in the Sac-Joaquin Section and first in San Joaquin County. But there’s more to the 5-foot-11 guard’s game than spot-up shooting. He’s a versatile perimeter threat who can score off stand-still looks, step-backs and ball screens. Mapanao averaged 14.5 points per game.
Jagger Merolla High School: Lincoln
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Lincoln may have lost its top two scorers from last year’s CIF Division I State Championship runner-up team, but the torch didn’t simply fall to Jagger Merolla — he was already built to carry it. At 6-foot-3 and 210 pounds, Merolla brings power, polish and personality. He can bully defenders on the block, step out for 3s, drop dimes and sprinkle in a little trash talk to keep the energy high. His swagger fuels Lincoln just as much as his production. Merolla averaged 11.3 points and nearly five rebounds last season. "Jagger is a workhorse that is ready to take the reins as one of the focal points of this team," Lincoln coach Anthony Matthews said, "A 3-year varsity starter, Jagger averaged over 20 points per game over the summer."
Jerimyah Owens High School: Weston Ranch
Position/Year: Forward, Junior
Summary: Jerimyah Owens is a returning SJAA first-team all-league selection. His scoring around the basket, combined with his strength, athleticism and improved shooting touch, should make him an even bigger threat than he was a year ago. His numbers as a sophomore weren’t eye-popping at 6.9 points per game, but his talent is obvious. Owens has already shown rapid growth on the AAU circuit with the Stockton Soldiers, highlighted by a 40-point game without hitting a jumper.
Anthony Rose-Garcia High School: Galt
Position/Year: Guard, Junior
Summary: Where would Galt be without Anthony Rose-Garcia? The Warriors went 1-27 last season, and the 5-foot-10 point guard was often the lone bright spot. He posted games of 35, 31, 28 and 27 points — twice — on his way to averaging 17.8 points per game.
Maximillian Russell High School: Tracy
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: Face-guard him, double him, chase him — Maximillian Russell still gets his. The 6-foot-1 Tracy guard erupted for 21.3 points per game last season and has a real case as not just one of the county’s best, but one of Northern California’s top guards. He scores from everywhere and has the bounce to finish with dunks when he gets a lane. This summer, Russell ran with Rip Hamilton’s City Elite program and battled on the EYBL, the premier grassroots stage in the country.
Tre Simmons High School: Lincoln
Position/Year: Guard, Sophomore
Summary: There’s no better way to put it: Tre Simmons is special. Truly, unmistakably special. The 6-foot-5 sophomore already owns a Division I offer from the University of the Pacific and has lived through more big stages than most players see by the end of their careers. He dissects defenses with methodical precision — controlled drives, smooth midrange pull-ups and sharp decision-making out of the post. When he has the ball, the tempo slows, the chaos fades and the right play emerges. Last season’s 7.1 points per game as a freshman barely scratched the surface; doubling that output feels well within reach.
Monte Shelton High School: Merrill West
Position/Year: Wing, Senior
Summary: Scoring comes naturally to Monte Shelton. His athletic ability pops right away, but it’s his feel for the game and smart decision-making that elevate him. Combine that with a confident handle and a clean, reliable jumper, and the 6-foot-2 wing becomes the type of player who can drop 15-plus without breaking stride. He earned MVP honors at both the West Holiday Tournament and the Clovis Elks Christmas Tournament during his first varsity season, then averaged 16 points per game to earn second-team All-TCAL and lead West to its first playoff appearance since 2017. After a strong summer with the Stockton Soldiers, he enters his senior season with momentum.
Sean Tetz High School: Lodi
Position/Year: Forward, Senior
Summary: In a basketball world obsessed with pace and space, Sean Tetz is bringing the back-to-the-basket game out of retirement. A bruiser — that’s who he is. A first-team TCAL tight end in football, he’s just as effective on the hardwood. He averaged 10 points and five rebounds last season, but with Lodi’s leading scorer gone, expect the offense to run through him in the post. Whether he’s backing defenders down or turning to face up, Tetz is reviving the old-school style.
Jake Vander Veen High School: Ripon Christian
Position/Year: Guard, Senior
Summary: On the ball, off the ball, it doesn’t matter — Jake Vander Veen produces. The 6-foot-3 senior spent last season piling up numbers — 19.2 points on 46.2% shooting, 5.1 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals — and somehow looked even better live than in the box score. He soared past the 1,000-point career mark and capped the year as the 2025 Trans Valley League MVP.
Alonzo Ward High School: Edison
Position/Year: Guard, Sophomore
Summary: Alonzo Ward looks like a future Division I football player — and possibly a Division I basketball player, too. He finished his second varsity football season with 826 yards and 11 touchdowns, and his transition to the court is somehow just as effortless. As a freshman last year, fresh off the varsity football field, Ward averaged nearly 12 points per game, the most of any freshman in San Joaquin County.
Jordan Williams High School: Mountain House
Position/Year: Center, Senior
Summary: Not many players at 6-foot-7 and 230 pounds have the footwork Jordan Williams does. A true big who can score on the block or step out and hit a pick-and-pop three, Williams is coming off a season in which he averaged eight points and five rebounds. With Mountain House’s top two scorers gone, his brute strength will get him points, but his improved post game should have the offense running through him even more.
